title: Weak or strong card sort
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming sequences and online safety
source: Seeded from computing/y3 lesson 6 (Weak or strong card sort (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 6: Powerful passwords. To understand what makes a password strong and why we keep it private

blocks.title: Sort into: Weak / Strong
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Weak, Strong.
blocks.answer: Weak: password; ali2017; 123456; football. Strong: CloudTeapotRiver; BlueLampOrange9

questions.a: No: it uses a name and a year, which are easy to guess.
questions.model: Teacher thinks aloud: 'Is it long? Quite. Could someone guess it? Yes, it is a name and a birth year. So it is weak.'

questions.q: Make 'catdog' stronger using the three random words rule.
Where must a password never be typed in a Teams lesson?
questions.a: In the chat (or anywhere others can see).

questions.q: Core: Write three random words that would make a strong password (do NOT use your real one).
questions.model: Teacher picks three things in the room that do not go together: 'Kettle, Moon, Sock: KettleMoonSock.'

questions.q: Extend: Write two rules for keeping a password private in the portal response box. Start: 'I will...'
questions.a: I will only share my password with my parents. I will never type it in the chat.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why 'BlueLampOrange9' is harder to guess than 'blue'.
questions.a: It is longer, uses three unrelated words, capitals and a number, so there are many more possibilities to try.

questions.q: Which is the strongest password? A) 123456 B) amina C) TigerSpoonCloud
Big question: who should have a copy of your password key?
questions.a: Only me and my parents (trusted adults at home).
